question: In an article published on 7 January 20241, the Journal du Dimanche asked why Luis Miguel Bueno, the EU’s Arabic spokesperson, was promoting Islam within the EU. Mr Bueno’s online posts are certainly surprising. On his official account, he posted ‘Happy Friday’ (the most important day of prayer for Muslims) with a photo of a mosque2.

He made a series of videos in mosques, praising his experience there as ‘one of the strongest spiritual moments of [his] life’3. He sang ‘Happy Ramadan’ from behind a lectern decorated in EU colours4. He published a report entitled ‘How the Holy Quran reached Europe’5. He participated in a Muslim Brotherhood rally praising ‘the significant role of the Arabic language in Europe’6.
These shocking communications and choices raise questions about his possible proximity to the networks of political Islam, or even his personal adherence to radical Islam. Can the Commission say: 1.
Whether it approves of the official communication by its spokesperson and, if it does not, remove him from office?
Whether it will cease all dialogue with Muslim Brotherhood networks and associations close to them, as well as with all NGOs linked to radical Islam?
Whether it will declare a moratorium and carry out a full audit of the subsidies – tens of millions of EU taxpayers’ money – granted to associations linked to political Islam and radical Islam?
answer: The function of the Regional Media Officer (RMO) is to communicate externally to Arabic-speaking audiences in the Middle East and North Africa in order to build trust and improve perception of the EU as a relatable partner through a combination of soft content (people-to-people approach) and more institutional and policy-related messages.

Similar models in like-minded partners are the United Kingdom Government Arabic Spokesperson for the Middle East and Northern Africa region (7), the Arabic Spokesperson for the United States State Department (8), Germany’s Arabic Spokesperson (9) or France’s Arabic Spokesperson (10).

The work of the RMO reflects the diverse and inclusive nature of the EU’s external communication, tailored to specific local contexts, showing respect and appreciation for the religious, cultural and social characteristics of the target audience. The reference to alleged participation of the RMO in a ‘Muslim Brotherhood rally’ is incorrect.

As part of his engagement with regional audiences, the RMO was invited to an event organised by the Islamic World Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (ICESCO) (11), an intergovernmental organisation not affiliated with the Muslim Brotherhood.

His video message on the occasion of the United Nations-designated Arabic Language Da y (12), which was screened during the event, recognises, inter alia, the significant role the Arabic language has played in developing European scholarship, with hundreds of scientific terms borrowed from Arabic across European languages.

The EU, together with its Member States, is actively engaged in the prevention of radicalisation and extremism, as well as the promotion of a culture of tolerance and respect for diversity. The Commission does not support any organisation that pursues an illegal or extremist agenda or does not fully respect fundamental rights and values.
